job.title: Human Resources Business Partner
job.description:
The employer
Junction Australia is a well-established South Australian not-for-profit organisation making a genuine difference in the lives of people across our community.

Supporting around 10,000 South Australians each year, Junction delivers a range of housing and community services, including programs supporting children, young people and families.

With a strong focus on its people and culture, Junction is committed to creating a workplace where employees feel supported, valued and empowered to do their best work.

The opportunity
This is a fantastic opportunity for someone who enjoys the more complex side of HR, particularly employee and industrial relations, and wants to continue building their skills in a role offering plenty of variety, challenge and the opportunity to make a difference.

Working closely with the HR Lead and alongside a genuinely lovely, supportive team, you'll partner with managers across the organisation, providing practical advice, coaching and guidance on a broad range of people matters.

A significant part of the role will involve navigating complex ER and IR issues, including workplace investigations, grievances, performance management and disciplinary matters. You'll need to be confident in your knowledge of employment legislation and comfortable working through challenging situations to achieve fair and practical outcomes.

There's also plenty of opportunity to get involved in HR projects, continuous improvement initiatives and broader people and culture activities. With the support of an HR Coordinator, you'll have the opportunity to focus on building strong relationships with managers and providing meaningful, hands-on HR support.

Some of your key responsibilities will include:

  • Partnering with managers to provide practical, solutions-focused HR advice and support
  • Managing complex employee and industrial relations matters, including workplace investigations, grievances and disciplinary processes
  • Coaching and supporting managers to build their confidence and capability in managing people
  • Providing advice on employment legislation, awards, workplace policies and performance management
  • Supporting organisational change, workforce planning and employee engagement initiatives
  • Contributing to HR projects and improvements to policies, systems and processes
  • Utilising Junction's new HRIS, Humanforce, to support HR processes and reporting

About you
We're looking for an experienced HR professional who has a strong foundation in employee and industrial relations and genuinely enjoys working through complex people matters.

You'll be someone who can build trust and credibility with managers, provide sound advice and isn't afraid to have the difficult conversations when needed. Just as importantly, you'll have a practical, approachable style and enjoy being part of a team that works closely together and supports one another.

Ideally, you'll bring:

  • Solid HR generalist experience, with particular strength in employee and industrial relations advisory
  • Confidence and demonstrated experience managing workplace investigations and complex employee matters
  • Strong knowledge of employment legislation, award interpretation and contemporary HR practices
  • Experience working in a complex organisation, ideally within a unionised environment
  • The ability to coach, influence and build positive working relationships with managers at all levels
  • Sound judgement, a solutions-focused approach and the confidence to manage sensitive matters independently
  • A collaborative approach and a genuine interest in contributing to a positive workplace culture

Previous experience in community services isn't essential. What matters most is that you've worked in an environment where you've been exposed to complex ER and IR matters and have the confidence and experience to navigate them effectively.

Experience working in a unionised environment will be highly regarded, as will familiarity with the SCHADS Award.

Why join Junction?
There's a lot to like about this opportunity!

Firstly, you'll be joining a great bunch of people who genuinely enjoy working together. The HR team is collaborative, supportive and passionate about what they do, and there's a real focus across Junction on creating a positive workplace culture.

You'll also have the opportunity to further develop your ER/IR expertise, work through interesting and challenging matters, and contribute to an organisation doing meaningful work in the community.

Some of the benefits include:

  • Flexible start and finish times and the option to work a compressed week (9-day fortnight)
  • Work from home one day per week
  • Beautiful new offices at Tonsley, with great facilities and onsite parking
  • Salary packaging benefits
  • Additional paid leave, including a 'You Are Amazing Day' and NAIDOC Day
  • Professional development opportunities and a strong focus on employee wellbeing

If you're an experienced HR professional who enjoys a challenge, values being part of a great team and would love the opportunity to contribute to an organisation making a genuine difference, we'd love to hear from you.

To apply, please submit your resume via the link provided. For a confidential discussion about the opportunity, contact the team at Mansfield & Co Recruitment.

job.title: Recruitment Associate
job.description:
Who's hiring?

Well, this time it's us!

Mansfield & Co is a boutique recruitment agency based on Unley Road in Malvern. We've been around for over 10 years and, in that time, have built some fantastic relationships with businesses and candidates across South Australia.

We're a small team with a big network, recruiting across Accounting & Finance, Office Support, HR, Marketing & Communications and senior leadership roles. Our clients are just as varied, from family-owned businesses and growing SMEs to some of SA's most recognised organisations.

We're pretty proud of the reputation we've built. We take our work seriously, but definitely not ourselves! We believe recruitment should be personal, honest and enjoyable, and we're big on doing the right thing by both our clients and candidates.

So, what's the opportunity?

We're creating a new Recruitment Associate role to support our growing team, and we're looking for someone who genuinely loves the candidate side of recruitment.

If you're someone who gets a real buzz out of meeting great people, uncovering talent and matching candidates with opportunities they'll love, this could be right up your alley.

You'll work closely with our consultants across permanent and temporary recruitment, sourcing, interviewing and building relationships with candidates at all levels.

One day you might be interviewing an Executive Assistant, the next a Finance Manager or HR professional. You'll also help us grow our busy temp desk, keep recruitment campaigns on track and make sure our candidates continue to receive a great experience.

It's a role with plenty of variety, lots of people interaction and the opportunity to make a genuine contribution to our team's success.

And while recruitment will be your main focus, we're a small team, so you'll also get involved in a bit of everything else that keeps M&Co ticking along!

What will your week look like?

No two weeks will be quite the same, but here's a taste of what you'll be doing:

  • Sourcing great candidates through LinkedIn, SEEK, our database and networks
  • Screening applications and conducting candidate interviews across a wide range of roles and industries
  • Building relationships with candidates and keeping in touch with great people for future opportunities
  • Supporting our consultants with recruitment campaigns, candidate shortlists, reference checks and pre-employment processes
  • Working alongside our Temp Consultant to source and onboard temporary staff, assist with urgent requirements and help manage timesheets
  • Spotting standout candidates to feature in our Talent Showcase and introduce to clients
  • Keeping our recruitment processes running smoothly when consultants are away
  • Helping coordinate team events, marketing activities and the general day-to-day running of the office

What are we looking for?

First and foremost, we're looking for someone who loves recruitment, enjoys talking to people and takes pride in doing a great job.

You'll already have recruitment experience and feel confident interviewing candidates independently. You'll be curious, a good listener and someone who can quickly get their head around different roles and what makes a great candidate.

You'll also be:

  • Organised, proactive and comfortable juggling a few things at once
  • A natural relationship builder who enjoys getting to know people
  • Tech-savvy and happy to embrace new tools, including AI, to work smarter
  • Detail-oriented, with good judgement and a commercial mindset
  • Flexible and willing to roll up your sleeves when things get busy
  • Someone who enjoys being part of a team and brings a level of energy and a positive attitude to work

Why join us?

We're a small, close-knit team and genuinely enjoy working together. We work hard, support each other and enjoy a good chat and a laugh throughout the day. We also love an excuse to get out for lunch, celebrate a win or organise a team activity.

And there's something exciting on the horizon! We're moving into a brand-new office on King William Road, Unley in early 2027.

You'll have the opportunity to work across a really interesting mix of recruitment assignments, build your skills and contribute ideas in an environment where everyone's input is valued.

We're also big believers in flexibility and understand that there's life outside of work. We're open to someone working full-time or part-time, with the option to work from home one day per week (if working full-time hours).

Sound like your kind of role?

If you love the candidate side of recruitment, enjoy variety and think you'd be a great addition to our team, we'd love to hear from you!

Send your resume and a cover letter telling us a little about yourself and why you'd like to join M&Co.

For a confidential chat, feel free to give Mel a call on 0411 471 822.

job.title: Finance and Payroll Officer
job.description:
Who's hiring?
Established in 1996, Penfield Food Co is a proudly South Australian, family-owned food manufacturer with a passion for quality gourmet products. What began with traditional table olives and olive oil, inspired by the family's Greek heritage, has grown into an extensive range of Mediterranean-inspired foods, including antipasto, marinated vegetables, tapenades, specialty vinegars and more.

Today, Penfield Food Co supplies retail and food service customers across Australia. With exciting plans for continued growth, the business remains true to its family values, commitment to quality and the people who have helped build its success.

So, what's the role?
We're looking for an experienced Finance and Payroll Officer to take ownership of the day-to-day financial administration that keeps Penfield Food Co running smoothly.

Working autonomously within a small, supportive team, you'll enjoy a varied role with the opportunity to contribute to reporting and business improvements as the company grows.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Accounts payable: Managing invoice processing, supplier reconciliations and preparing payments for approval.
  • Payroll: Processing weekly payroll for approximately 14 employees, including timesheets, leave entitlements and employee records.
  • Accounts receivable: Providing support with invoicing, customer accounts and payment enquiries, particularly on Fridays and during leave periods.
  • Financial administration: Completing data entry, bank reconciliations, month-end processes and maintaining accurate records in MYOB AccountRight.
  • Business reporting: Preparing reports on cost of goods, sales performance and other financial information to support business decisions.
  • General office support: Assisting with phone enquiries and administration, alongside providing information to the external accountant for financial reporting and compliance.

You'll have the independence to manage your responsibilities, with support from an external accountant, bookkeeper and accounts receivable team member.

What are we looking for?
You're an experienced accounts professional who takes pride in accuracy, enjoys working independently and can be relied upon to keep things running smoothly. You're comfortable managing competing priorities and appreciate the collaborative, hands-on nature of a family business.

You'll bring:

  • Proven experience in accounts, bookkeeping or a similar finance administration role.
  • Confidence managing accounts payable, payroll and reconciliations.
  • Proficiency in MYOB AccountRight and Excel, with excellent attention to detail.
  • Strong organisational skills and the ability to work autonomously.
  • A proactive, practical approach and friendly communication style.

Experience in FMCG or manufacturing, along with an interest in financial reporting and analysis, would be an advantage.

Formal qualifications aren't essential. We're looking for someone with the right experience, attitude and ability to become a valued member of the team.

What's in it for you?
This is a great opportunity to enjoy the stability of an established family business, with attractive remuneration, flexibility and the independence to manage your work.

  • Permanent part-time hours: Enjoy a consistent Tuesday to Friday schedule, working 25–28 hours per week.
  • Flexible start times: Some flexibility to arrange your working hours around your commitments.
  • Attractive remuneration: A competitive package that recognises your experience and contribution.
  • Autonomy and variety: Take ownership of your responsibilities and enjoy a mix of accounts, payroll and reporting.
  • A supportive workplace: Join a welcoming, established team where your contribution is valued.
  • An exciting future: Be part of a successful local business with plans for continued growth.

How do I apply?
If you fit the brief and are excited by the opportunity to contribute to a great local business who is doing their bit for the world, we can't wait to hear from you.

For a confidential discussion, contact Tracy Frankenfeld at Mansfield & Co on 0493 703 697 or tracy@mansfieldandco.com.au

#SCR-tracy-frankenfeld

job.title: Finance Officer
job.description:
Finance Officer | Temporary Contract

We’re partnering with an established South Australian not-for-profit that makes a difference in the community. It’s a dynamic and exciting place to work, and this is a great opportunity to put your finance skills to use in a small team where your work will make a day-to-day difference.
They’re looking for an experienced Finance Officer who enjoys getting to know the people and operations behind the numbers.

So, what’s the role?

Reporting to the Senior Finance and Business Partner, you’ll take care of fortnightly payroll and accounts payable and help keep month-end on track. There’s a good mix of work here, from checking the details of a pay run and getting supplier payments out on time to preparing accruals and helping pull together the monthly financial reports.

Here’s what a typical week might look like:

  • Processing fortnightly payroll in Xero, including leave, allowances and reimbursements
  • Coding and processing supplier invoices, reconciling statements and preparing payment runs
  • Completing bank and payroll clearing account reconciliations and following up on discrepancies
  • Preparing accruals and helping get the accounts ready for month-end
  • Supporting the preparation of monthly financial reports
  • Responding to payroll and accounts queries from staff and suppliers

Enough about us - let’s talk about whether this role is for you!

You’re comfortable keeping track of a few deadlines at once and happy to follow things up when the numbers don’t quite add up.

We’d love to hear from you if you bring experience in any of the following areas, with payroll and accounts payable central to the role.

  • Processing payroll and managing accounts payable
  • Preparing accruals, completing reconciliations and supporting month-end reporting
  • Using Xero and Excel in a finance role

A current Working with Children Check and police clearance are required for this assignment.

If you’re available to start ASAP, apply with your CV or get in touch with Jacqui Davey at Mansfield & Co Recruitment for a confidential chat.

job.title: Financial Accountant
job.description:
Who's hiring?
Centacare is one of South Australia's most trusted not-for-profits, supporting more than 20,000 South Australians each year. We're there for people doing it tough - whether they're navigating mental health challenges, domestic and family violence, homelessness, disability services, carer support or relationship breakdown. We show up with serious heart, vital services and relentless compassion.

Core to providing that support - consistently, sustainably and with impact - is our finance team. And right now, we're looking for a Financial Accountant who's ready to roll up their sleeves and make a difference.

So, what's the role?
This is a fantastic opportunity for a Financial Accountant who enjoys getting into the detail, takes pride in getting the numbers right and likes being part of a collaborative finance team.

Reporting to the Finance Manager, you'll be responsible for key financial accounting activities, including month-end processes, general ledger management, balance sheet reconciliations and payroll journals. You'll play an important role in ensuring the accuracy and integrity of financial information, maintaining strong financial controls and keeping reporting deadlines on track.

Working closely with the broader finance team, including Finance Business Partners, payroll and operational teams, you'll also have the opportunity to contribute to process improvements and systems enhancements across the organisation.

Here's what a typical week might look like:

  • Managing the general ledger and preparing monthly balance sheet reconciliations
  • Coordinating month-end processes, including accruals, journals and ensuring reporting deadlines are met
  • Preparing payroll journals and reconciliations, working closely with payroll and HR to resolve discrepancies
  • Managing fixed asset and depreciation schedules, along with grant income recognition
  • Assisting with year-end statutory accounts and liaising with internal and external auditors
  • Supporting the broader finance team and identifying opportunities to improve financial processes and systems

Enough about us—let's talk about whether this role is for you!
You're a detail-oriented Accountant who enjoys the technical side of accounting and takes pride in producing accurate, reliable financial information. You're organised, comfortable working to deadlines and have a knack for identifying discrepancies and working through problems.

Importantly, you're someone who thinks critically, asks questions and has the confidence to make decisions rather than simply following processes. You'll enjoy being hands-on, but you're also someone who sees the bigger picture and understands the importance of strong financial processes and controls.

Technically speaking, you:

  • Hold a degree in Accounting, Finance or Business (or equivalent experience)
  • Have solid experience in financial accounting, particularly month-end processes, general ledger management and balance sheet reconciliations
  • Have a sound understanding of accounting principles and standards, including accrual accounting, income recognition and lease accounting
  • Bring strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills, with the confidence to investigate issues and make informed decisions
  • Have advanced Excel skills and enjoy working with complex financial data
  • Are highly organised, detail-oriented and comfortable working to deadlines
  • Communicate confidently with stakeholders, including internal and external auditors
  • Experience with TechnologyOne will be highly regarded
  • Hold (or are willing to obtain) a valid DHS Working with Children Check

What's in it for you?

  • A chance to do meaningful work in an organisation that helps thousands of South Australians
  • The opportunity to join a collaborative and supportive finance team
  • Career development, mentoring and ongoing learning opportunities
  • Hybrid working (WFH one day a week)
  • Access to NFP salary packaging benefits

Sound like your kind of role?
Click that apply button - we'd love to hear from you. Have further questions? Give Melanie at Mansfield & Co a call on 0411 471 822 for a confidential chat.

job.title: Business Performance & Commercial Analyst
job.description:
Who's hiring?
ForestrySA is a unique South Australian organisation with a lot more happening behind the scenes than you might expect!

Managing some of South Australia's most beautiful forests, ForestrySA's operations span commercial forestry, conservation, tourism, recreation and community education. From sustainable timber production to walking and mountain biking trails, campgrounds and school education programs, their work is incredibly diverse.

With an ambitious growth agenda and plenty of exciting opportunities on the horizon, it's a great time to join the business.

The office location is pretty special too! Based in the beautiful Kuitpo Forest, you'll be surrounded by stunning scenery and wildlife, with the opportunity to enjoy a forest walk on your lunch break.

So, what's the role?
Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, this newly created position will play an important role in supporting ForestrySA's growth plans and improving commercial decision-making across the business.

It's a hands-on, commercially focused role where you'll work closely with operational managers and the leadership team, providing the financial modelling, analysis and insights needed to assess opportunities, develop business cases and improve business performance.

You'll be involved in a broad range of projects and initiatives, with plenty of variety and the opportunity to make a genuine contribution.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Developing financial models, business cases and commercial evaluations to support new initiatives and investment decisions.
  • Analysing financial and operational performance, identifying trends, opportunities and areas for improvement.
  • Preparing cost-benefit analyses, forecasts and scenario modelling to support business planning.
  • Developing meaningful performance reports, dashboards and KPIs to support management decisions.
  • Working closely with managers across the business to understand operational challenges and identify commercial opportunities.
  • Supporting strategic projects, process improvements and initiatives designed to improve efficiency and business performance.
  • Preparing commercial insights and recommendations for the CFO, leadership team and Board.

What are we looking for?
We're looking for a commercially minded finance professional who enjoys getting into the detail, solving problems and working closely with people across a business.

Ideally, you'll be CA or CPA qualified, with experience in commercial analysis, financial modelling, business case development or a similar commercially focused finance role.

You'll bring:

  • Strong financial modelling and advanced Excel skills, with the ability to analyse complex information and develop practical recommendations.
  • Experience preparing business cases, commercial evaluations and performance reporting.
  • Well-developed analytical, critical thinking and problem-solving skills.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the confidence to build relationships across all levels of a business.
  • A proactive, resourceful approach – you're comfortable asking questions, seeking out information and working through challenges.
  • The flexibility and adaptability to thrive in an evolving environment where priorities and opportunities may change.

Experience with Power BI would be advantageous, although it's not essential.
Just as importantly, you'll be personable, curious and collaborative. You'll enjoy getting out from behind your desk, understanding how different parts of the business operate and working with others to achieve great outcomes.

What's in it for you?
There's a lot to like about this opportunity. You'll be joining a supportive, collaborative team at a time when ForestrySA is looking to grow, innovate and explore new commercial opportunities.

As a newly created position, there's genuine scope to make the role your own, contribute ideas and have a direct impact on business decisions.
You'll also enjoy a unique working environment at Kuitpo Forest, with the flexibility to work from home one to two days per week.

How to apply
If you're looking for a commercially focused role with plenty of variety and the opportunity to contribute to an organisation that plays an important role in South Australia, we'd love to hear from you.

To apply, send your cover letter and resume by clicking APPLY below and we’ll handle the rest! For a confidential discussion, contact Melanie at Mansfield & Co on 0411 471 822.
